marks.gloss_en: בשלמא רב הונא כשמעתיה -- the animal stands in a presumption of prohibition
רב חסדא מאי טעמא? אמר לך: a doubt does not remove a certainty
a bone certainly notches, hide may or may not; it is doubt against certainty, and a doubt does not remove a certainty
מתיב רבא לסיועיה לרב הונא -- the immersion baraita, where doubt removes certainty
מתיב רבא: he certainly immersed, the interposition is doubtful -- and the doubt removes the certainty
one immersed and an interposition was found on him -- even if he handled that kind all day, the immersion fails until he says 'I am sure it was not on me before'
שאני התם: the impure man has his own presumption of impurity (the later הכא נמי rounds leave this standing)
שאני התם: one can say, establish the impure man on his presumption and say he did not immerse
הכא נמי: establish the animal on its presumption [of prohibition] and say it was not slaughtered (against a_haamed_tamei_al_chezkato's logic)
הרי שחוטה לפניך -- the slaughtered animal is before you
הכא נמי: he has immersed before you! -- reinstating Rava's parallel against the previous answer
הא איתיילידא ביה ריעותא -- a flaw (the interposition) arose in him
הכא נמי איתיילידא בה ריעותא -- here too a flaw arose (the notch)
סכין איתרעאי, בהמה לא איתרעאי (= p_sakin_itrea)
the knife was flawed; the animal was not flawed
מיתיבי: 'every doubt in slaughter is invalid' -- does it not include the notched knife?
the baraita: he cut the gullet and afterwards the windpipe was displaced -- valid
לא, לאתויי ספק שהה ספק דרס (= p_kol_safek_leatuyei_shehiya)
'every doubt in slaughter' -- does it not come to include a case like this one (the notched knife)?
Rav Huna: one who slaughtered with a knife later found notched -- even if he broke bones with it all day -- the slaughter is invalid
where he does not know whether the windpipe was displaced before or after -- that was the case, and they said: every doubt in slaughter is invalid
אי נמי: found as he left it, there is neither impurity nor disqualification -- ואילו ספק מים מגולים אסורין, שמע מינה חמירא סכנתא מאיסורא
but found as he left it -- there is neither impurity nor disqualification
from the Para mishna: doubts of impurity/disqualification are sometimes resolved leniently, while doubtfully-exposed water is always forbidden -- שמע מינה חמירא סכנתא מאיסורא
ישתה? הא קא חזי ליה! -- if it only comes out from under the handle and drinks, he would see it
אלא ישתה ויחזור לחורו (= p_yishteh_veyachzor)
rather: [long enough to come out,] drink, and return to its hole
R' Yehoshua b. Levi: what is the reason [found uncovered is not impure]? because creeping things' way is to uncover, not to cover
three liquids are forbidden on account of exposure: water, wine and milk
